title: GS Caltex to Supply 2,000 Tons of Sustainable Aviation Fuel to DHL Express - 아시아경제
content:
GS Caltex to Supply 2,000 Tons of Sustainable Aviation Fuel to DHL Express GS Caltex will supply Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) to DHL Express, a global international express company. Kim Changsoo, Vice President of Mobility & Marketing at GS Caltex, and John Pearson, CEO of DHL Express, signed a Memorandum of Understanding for a "Partnership to Build Carbon Reduction Based on Sustainable Aviation Fuel" on the 8th at the GS Tower in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, and took a commemorative photo. GS Caltex GS Caltex announced on September 9 that on the previous day, at GS Tower in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, Vice President Kim Changsoo of the Mobility & Marketing Division at GS Caltex and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) John Pearson of DHL Express, along with other key officials from both companies, signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on "Establishing a Partnership for Carbon Reduction Based on Sustainable Aviation Fuel." Under this agreement, GS Caltex will supply SAF to DHL Express aircraft refueling in Korea for one year. The supply volume will be 2,000 tons of neat SAF (100% SAF). The SAF supplied by GS Caltex is produced using a co-processing method, which involves connecting a separate bio-based feedstock supply line to the existing petroleum product manufacturing process to create low-carbon products. It has also obtained International Sustainability and Carbon Certification (ISCC) EU certification, in accordance with the European Union (EU) Renewable Energy Directive. GS Caltex plans to establish a dedicated co-processing production line for the stable and expanded supply of SAF to meet market demand by the end of this year. GS Caltex has been supplying internationally certified SAF produced by the co-processing method to Asiana Airlines, Jin Air, and Eastar Jet since December 2024. Additionally, it has supplied Korean Air since September last year and Aero K Airlines since December last year. © The Asia Business Daily. All rights reserved. title: The Japanese Luxury Sedan That Could Actually Challenge BMW - HotCars
content: Eric Tipan has spent more than 30 years working across journalism, broadcasting and live media. He’s a five-time Henry Ford Award winner, has covered the Olympic Games for TV5 and One Sports, called international volleyball for Volleyball World, and written and presented automotive stories for AutoIndustriya.com and Manila Bulletin. Before that, radio was a big part of his career. Nearly 25 years of it, as a presenter, program director and production lead. That range shows up in the way he works. Whether he’s writing, editing or speaking live on air, Eric has a knack for making technical or fast-moving subjects easier to understand without stripping away the detail that makes them interesting. Subscribe to the HotCars newsletter to never miss an update For years, the luxury sedan shorthand was easy. Buy German if you wanted steering feel and a chassis that seemed to enjoy an empty on-ramp as much as you did. Buy Japanese if you wanted something quieter, calmer, and less likely to make you send your service adviser a Facebook friend request. One sedan made that division much less tidy. It had a naturally aspirated V6, rear-wheel drive, adaptive dampers, 19-inch performance tires, larger brakes, quick steering, and even available rear-wheel steering. Contemporary testing showed the hardware wasn't there just to fill a brochure. The F Sport's case was made underneath the body. Lexus fitted firmer springs, thicker anti-roll bars, revised bushings, adaptive dampers, and quicker variable-ratio steering. Rear-drive cars also got staggered 19-inch performance tires, which gave the GS considerably more cornering intent than the typical Japanese executive sedan of the period. The available rear-steering system added another layer. Lexus said the system could turn the rear wheels opposite the fronts at lower speeds and, in certain conditions above 50 mph, in the same direction to improve agility and stability. On the road, the idea was simple: make a fairly large sedan feel less reluctant to turn and more settled once the speed came up. Car and Driver found out just how much of that hardware translated to the pavement. The rear-drive performance model reached 60 mph in 5.5 seconds, pulled 0.89 g on the skidpad, and stopped from 70 mph in 160 feet, while running within a tenth of a second of a contemporary BMW 535i to 60 mph. Those results came from Car and Driver's instrumented test of the fourth-generation car. The steering wasn't perfect. And “BMW handling” certainly doesn't mean the GS beat BMW at its own game. Car and Driver still described the steering feel as synthetic even while praising the car's grip, brakes, and high handling limits. BMW was simply a credible benchmark for this sedan, which was already a pretty surprising place for this particular Japanese luxury brand to find itself. The mystery sedan is the fourth-generation Lexus GS 350 F Sport, launched for the 2013 model year. And no, this wasn't an IS F with a quieter exhaust or a regular GS wearing an angry body kit. It was Lexus's midsize luxury sedan with enough real chassis work to truly deserve the F Sport badge. At launch, the GS 350 used a 3.5-liter naturally aspirated V6 producing 306 horsepower and 277 lb-ft of torque. Rear-wheel drive and all-wheel drive were both available, while the 2013 rear-drive version used a six-speed automatic with paddle shifters, quicker shifts, and throttle blips on downshifts. The F Sport badge went considerably deeper than wheels and trim. It brought F Sport-tuned Adaptive Variable Suspension, firmer springs, thicker anti-roll bars, revised bushings, 19-inch wheels, and larger front brakes on rear-drive cars, while Sport S+ sharpened the adaptive suspension, steering, and powertrain settings. Edmunds found that the changes worked, praising quick turn-in, rapid transitions, good balance, and plenty of adjustability during its track testing. Yet it still had to be a GS. Testers found the F Sport comfortable enough to work as a proper executive sedan despite the sharper chassis. Edmunds' track test and Car and Driver's review both landed on roughly the same point: the car got much sharper without turning every expansion joint into a personal attack. A used sports sedan can be cheap to buy and spectacularly expensive to keep. The Lexus badge suddenly becomes much more relevant once the car is a decade old. Strong handling numbers don't mean much if the car spends every other weekend sitting on top of a car lift. The GS 350 F Sport's appeal is that its reputation doesn't begin and end with what it can do on the track. J.D. Power gives the 2013 Lexus GS 350 an 89/100 Quality & Reliability score and lists the model as a Dependability Award winner. Consumer Reports also rates some later fourth-generation GS models well for reliability. It says the 2014 GS is more reliable than most cars from that year, while the 2015 GS is much more reliable than its peers. Put together, those ratings give the GS's reliability reputation more than just a Lexus badge to lean on. The 2013 car complicates the story a little. Consumer Reports currently rates it about average for reliability compared with other cars from the same model year, so calling every fourth-generation GS "bulletproof" would be doing the car no favors. Its 2013 GS reliability page is a good reminder that Lexus reliability doesn't repeal the laws of aging, maintenance, or previous-owner creativity. None of these cars are young anymore, and F Sport versions have more chassis hardware to inspect than a basic luxury sedan. A pre-purchase inspection should cover the service history, suspension and steering, adaptive damping, electronics, infotainment, wheels and tires, and any evidence of leaks or neglected maintenance. A GS 350 F Sport can still break, especially after more than a decade on the road. What makes it appealing is that its reliability record makes the usual old-luxury-car gamble look a little less frightening. The GS 350 F Sport feels more unusual now than it did in 2013. Back then, a naturally aspirated V6, rear-wheel drive, a conventional automatic, and adaptive suspension weren't especially exotic ingredients in a luxury sedan. Today, that combination is getting hard to find. The GS competed with cars such as the BMW 5 Series, Mercedes-Benz E-Class, Audi A6, Cadillac CTS, Infiniti M/Q70, and Acura RL/RLX. Some of those nameplates have disappeared, others have changed direction, and the segment itself has been squeezed by crossovers, electrification, downsized turbo engines, and increasingly software-heavy luxury cars. Against today's luxury market, the old GS suddenly has more character than its 2013 spec sheet suggested. Depreciation strengthens the case, although current asking prices should always be checked close to publication because mileage, condition, drivetrain, and model year move the numbers around substantially. A comparable BMW may still give a purist more steering feel or a broader engine menu, while a standard Lexus might suit someone who has never once wondered what a skidpad number means. The GS 350 F Sport sits between those two ideas, which is exactly why it works. Lexus eventually ended GS production in 2020 after four generations, leaving this particular combination without a direct successor. That makes the fourth-generation F Sport feel more significant now than when it was simply another new luxury sedan competing for showroom space. Does it handle exactly like a BMW 5 Series? No. The better question is how many used luxury sedans can still give you this much grip, comfort, naturally aspirated power, and Lexus durability in the same car. We want to hear from you. title: Karol G’s ‘Bby Wow’ Briefly Dethrones a Historic No. 1 Hit on Apple Music - Remezcla
content: VATICAN CITY, VATICAN - SEPTEMBER 13: Karol G attends the "Grace For The World" event at St. Peter's Square on September 13, 2025 in Vatican City, Vatican. (Photo by Daniele Venturelli/Getty Images for Grace For The World) Karol G has pulled off a chart feat many thought unlikely: ending Ella Langley’s reign at No. 1. Over Labor Day weekend, the Colombian singer knocked “Choosin’ Texas” from the top of the U.S. Apple Music all-genre songs chart. Her single “BbY WOW,” a collaboration with Spanish artists Judeline and Rusowsky, rose to No. 1, dethroning Langley’s country-pop smash after one of the longest runs in chart history. “Choosin’ Texas” has spent much of 2026 looking like a permanent fixture at the top. Langley’s song has dominated across virtually every major measure of U.S. music consumption. On the Billboard Hot 100, “Choosin’ Texas” reached its 20th week at No. 1 on the chart dated Sept. 5, making it the longest-running non-holiday song in the history of the 68-year-old chart. Only Mariah Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas Is You,” with 22 weeks, has spent more time at No. 1. The song has also logged historic runs on multiple charts while becoming one of the year’s defining crossover country hits. By late August, it had already spent 16 weeks at No. 1 on Digital Song Sales and 17 weeks atop Streaming Songs. That makes Karol G’s Apple Music upset more than just another chart shuffle. It’s significant because listeners chose a different rhythm to close out the summer-long weekend. Beyond the U.S. Apple Music charts, “BbY WOW” has also surged internationally, reaching No. 1 on Apple Music’s global chart and Spotify’s Global Top 50, while topping Billboard’s Hot Latin Songs chart. Still, the upset wasn’t permanent. As of today (Tuesday, Sept. 8), “BbY WOW” has slipped to No. 2. Even so, the significance is clear: “BbY WOW” did what most songs in 2026 haven’t managed so far—and that’s a victory worth recognizing and celebrating. For Goldman Sachs, long regarded as a bellwether for Wall Street's guidance, underwriting, and trading businesses, the pullback arrived even as the firm's capital-markets franchise continued generating headlines, from a marquee stabilization mandate tied to a closely watched technology listing to a broader push into digital-asset settlement alongside a roster of global banking peers. The session's driver was a jobs report that came in firmer than most market watchers had penciled in, reviving talk that the Federal Reserve could tighten its stance further rather than ease it, a scenario that had seemed increasingly unlikely earlier in the year. Bond markets moved quickly, with yields on government debt climbing as traders repriced the odds of another rate hike, a shift that tends to pressure bank shares in the near term even when it eventually supports the net interest margins those same banks earn on loans and securities. Goldman Sachs, with a business mix skewed more toward capital-markets activity, wealth management, and trading than toward traditional deposit-taking, tends to react to rate-path shifts differently than more retail-focused peers. Higher yields can complicate fixed-rate trading conditions in the short run, yet a steeper rate path over time often widens the spread banks earn on client balances, a dynamic that market participants continue to weigh as they gauge how the latest data shift affects diversified banks headed into the back half of the year. The firm's guidance arm regularly ranks among the busiest in arranging mergers, acquisitions, and public offerings, while its trading operations span equities, fixed-rate instruments, currencies, and commodities. Beyond the marquee dealmaking business, Goldman Sachs has spent recent years broadening its asset and wealth management arm, aiming to build steadier, fee-based revenue streams that complement the inherently uneven cadence of guidance and underwriting work. That diversification push has reshaped how market participants view the firm, shifting the narrative from a pure trading and guidance shop toward a broader diversified financial institution with multiple engines of growth. Such mandates, while not guaranteed until formally finalized, tend to reinforce a bank's standing among the small handful of institutions capable of managing the most complex, highly anticipated public offerings. Separately, Goldman Sachs is among more than a dozen major global banks organizing a joint venture aimed at issuing a dollar-linked digital settlement instrument, a push that would extend the firm's footprint into digital-asset infrastructure alongside traditional guidance and trading lines. The initiative, still in its early planning stages, reflects how established banks are moving to shape emerging payment rails rather than cede that ground to newer entrants. Another trend involves the steady push toward fee-based, less capital-intensive revenue streams, a shift that has pushed Goldman Sachs and similar firms to expand wealth and asset management arms even as guidance and trading remain the more recognized parts of the business. That diversification effort aims to smooth out the historically uneven, deal-cycle-dependent nature of Wall Street earnings. That positioning has become a recurring theme in how the firm frames its own narrative to market participants and the broader public. That said, the diversified structure does not eliminate sensitivity to broad market conditions, as the day's pullback across financial shares demonstrated. Operationally, Goldman Sachs has continued emphasizing efficiency alongside growth, a balance that has become increasingly common across large Wall Street institutions as they weigh the costs of maintaining sprawling trading and guidance operations against the fee revenue those businesses generate. Technology spending, including efforts tied to digital-asset infrastructure and settlement rails, forms part of that broader efficiency push. Diversified banks including Goldman Sachs continue to navigate a list of familiar exposures, from shifting Federal Reserve rate expectations to regulatory scrutiny to competitive pressure from both traditional peers and newer, technology-driven entrants. The latest jobs data adds a fresh layer of uncertainty to that list, as market participants reassess how a firmer labor market and higher yields might reshape the rate path over coming quarters. Regulatory factors also remain a constant backdrop for firms of Goldman Sachs's size and systemic footprint, with capital and liquidity requirements shaping how much flexibility the firm has to expand its balance sheet, return capital to stockholders, or pursue new lines of business such as digital-asset settlement. Goldman Sachs competes across multiple fronts simultaneously, facing rival Wall Street firms in guidance and underwriting, larger universal banks in trading and financing, and a growing field of independent wealth managers in the fee-based guidance space. That multi-front competitive landscape has pushed the firm to defend its standing in traditional strongholds while also building out newer, faster-growing business lines. Goldman Sachs has long cultivated a reputation for recruiting and retaining top talent across trading, guidance, and wealth management, a competitive advantage the firm has worked to preserve even as compensation costs across Wall Street have climbed. Goldman Sachs has continued balancing capital return to stockholders through dividends and buyback activity against the need to maintain a sturdy balance sheet capable of supporting its trading and underwriting commitments. title: How Employers Are Thinking About Employee Stock Purchase Plans in 2026 - Goldman Sachs

For employers considering an ESPP or thinking about restructuring, there are a number of regulatory, financial, and employee attraction and retention considerations. This article shares insights into how employers are responding to these pressures and the trends shaping the broader market. From an employer’s perspective, an employee stock purchase plan can be a strategic compensation benefit helping to directly align employees’ financial incentives with those of shareholders and the business. At the time of this report, a slight majority of employers offer an ESPP (52%).1 This decision often hinges on several considerations, including the strength of ownership culture across the workforce, how closely participation tracks market-standard rates, the expense borne by the company, and the cash flow available to employees. The data shows meaningful differences in ESPP adoption by industry. Employers in the Technology, Media, & Telecommunications industry had the highest rate of ESPP availability (68%), while employers in the Real Estate sector were least likely to offer ESPPs (17%). This range suggests that employers weigh factors such as industry-specific talent dynamics, capital structure, and compensation philosophy when deciding whether to offer the benefit. While employers use a number of metrics to define eligible participants for ESPPs, the most common is hours worked per week (36%). This can effectively remove part-time workers from eligibility pools. Tenure (32%) is also frequently used to limit participation eligibility. This can help encourage loyalty and support employee retention efforts. Exactly half of the plans reviewed apply a single metric to limit employee eligibility, indicating a preference for administrative simplicity. 32% of employers take a two-metric approach, while the remaining 18% utilize three limitations. Employers that offer ESPPs fall into one of three broad plan structures: Qualified Section 423 plans, nonqualified plans, and direct purchase plans. Qualified plans made up the largest share of plans reviewed (76%), while nonqualified (14%) and direct purchase plans (10%) appeared less frequently but may offer practical advantages for certain employer objectives. Qualified Section 423 plans (76%) may be particularly appealing to employers because of the potential tax benefits they can provide to eligible US employees. At the same time, they require strict regulatory compliance, shareholder approval, nondiscrimination rules, and the annual statutory purchase limit ($25,000 per participant). Nonqualified plans represent a smaller share of ESPPs reviewed (14%) but employers are looking at the design as an option that introduces more flexibility, eases administrative needs, and simplifies tax treatment.  Because these plans are not subject to the same Section 423 framework, they can support a broader range of eligibility rules and incentive structures. This may be particularly relevant for multinational employers looking for a more consistent employee experience across jurisdictions. * Purchase Discounts are offered by the remaining 22% of employers. 40% of those employers that offer purchase discounts set the discount at 5%. This is not meant to be representative of the most common holistic nonqualified plan structure. Direct purchase plans were the least common structure offered by employers (10%). These plans can provide a simpler way for employees to buy company stock, but they generally offer fewer plan-design levers and potential tax planning opportunities than qualified or nonqualified ESPPs. This is not meant to be representative of the most common holistic direct purchase plan structure. For employers, the right ESPP design will depend on how the benefit fits into the broader total rewards strategy. Eligibility rules, offering frequency, contribution limits, incentive structure, and pricing methodology can all affect how employees interact with the plan and how the employer manages cost, administration, and alignment with business priorities. title: Lunchbreak: ‘Where Every Team Stands’ as 2026 Kickoff Weekend Arrives - Minnesota Vikings
content: The season begins tomorrow with a Super Bowl LX rematch. It continues Thursday in Australia between the Rams and the 49ers. And on Sunday, Minnesota hosts Green Bay in the 132nd Border Battle. It seems like an opportune time to assess where each team stands heading into the 2026 slate. That's exactly what Albert Breer did for Sports Illustrated this week. Here's what Breer wrote about the Purple in his check-in on the 32 clubs: The Vikings have had a reputation for being a great home for veteran quarterbacks that fell out of favor elsewhere, for one reason or another. It goes back to my childhood: Rich Gannon, Jim McMahon, Warren Moon, Randall Cunningham, Jeff George, Brett Favre and Kirk Cousins have all led Minnesota to the playoffs. Now they have Kyler Murray in to lead an offense with a ton of talent in the prime of their careers, with a veteran defense capable of maximizing Brian Flores's scheme. Note: Gannon was drafted by New England in 1987 but joined Minnesota that season. View photos of the Vikings 53-man roster as of Sep. 5, 2026. Breer noted that it's common for prognosticators to oversimplify things, insinuating that adding Murray to the mix is a solve-all for the franchise — "as if the quarterback is playing one-on-one hoops against the other team's quarterback," Breer wrote — but in this case there's some truth to it. Breer sees Murray being "that pivotal of a piece" and he highlighted Minnesota's confidence in the 29-year-old quarterback to bring dynamism to the offense on bootlegs, keepers and scramble drills. What else grabbed our attention in Breer's notebook? Well, thoughts on early season challengers. On the Packers, Breer conjectured that "this is already a good team. If its young guys can take the step from good to great, a la Seattle last year, then the Packers will be a true Super Bowl contender." As for Minnesota's opponents in Weeks 2 and 3 (Chicago and Tampa Bay) Breer focused on the respective quarterbacks: He cited his recent QB poll as proof that many people are expecting Caleb Williams to make a leap in his second season under Head Coach Ben Johnson; and Breer wondered whether there's still a deal to be done between the Buccaneers and Baker Mayfield, who is 27-24 in three seasons as Tampa Bay's starter and is second in the league with 95 passing TDs since 2023. Click here to read all of Breer's notes regarding the imminent campaign. Long before Vikings assistant defensive backs coach Chenzo Funari worked on Brian Flores' defense, he worked in a World War II-era garage in the Mojave Desert … on small rocket engines. Funari is the 32-year-old "secret weapon" who was profiled recently by The Athletic's Alec Lewis. The story of Funari's transition from science to the sidelines started in Southern California, in the middle of nowhere, before progressing into a volunteer coaching position at Youngstown State and landing him, eventually, in "a meaningful role on one of the most respected defensive staffs in the NFL." As a child, Funari fixated on two things: space and sports. He studied constellations. At the dinner table, he quizzed his parents on the solar system. (His sister) Taylor still doesn't know the answer to a question he'd constantly pose when he entered the living room: What is the average temperature on Mars? "It was like he was a walking encyclopedia," she said. The Cleveland native also adored the playing style of Hall of Fame quarterback Brett Favre. Maybe it was the fearlessness, possibly the flair. Funari practiced youth football with the gunslinger on his mind. His parents quickly recognized the sport was one of the few activities that gave his brain a break. Funari is entering his third season with the Vikings in 2026 and his second as a member of the coaching staff after joining the organization as a football quantitative methods associate. Although his background is unique, it serves him well. Players, including Harrison Smith, have gravitated toward his expertise. title: IPFT GS brutally assaulted by Tipra Motha supporters, car vandalised - Tripuratimes
content: Senior IPFT leader and party General Secretary Swapan Debbarma was brutally attacked and his car was vandalised allegedly by the activists of Tipra Motha Party in front of Hezamara block. The unprovoked attack was launched when Debbarma parked his car and was about to enter the block office to meet the RO. He said as soon as his car stopped by the block office, the assailants launched an unprovoked attack. The armed miscreants vandalised the car when he was inside it. His driver dodging the blows managed to contact the cops guarding the block office. The police personnel reached the spot immediately to rescue him. But, when he was being rescued from the spot, he suffered head injuries. According to Debbarma, when he tried to tell the Tipra Motha workers that he was a leader of the IPFT, a party that is in alliance with Tipra Motha, the severity and intensity of the attack increased. “I am clueless as to why my car was targeted. I thought they were mistaken to recognise me. When I tried to alert them that I am a senior leader of IPFT, the intensity of attack increased as if it didn't bother them at all,” said Debbarma. After being rescued, he was shifted to Mohanpur hospital where initial treatment was provided. For advanced treatment, he was referred to GB pant hospital’s trauma care centre. He was so severely injured that this entire shirt had stains of blood. IPFT leader and Minister Shukla Charan Noatia who went to the GB Pant hospital to inquire about his health. He condemned the incident and termed it “unacceptable”. “This kind of violence is completely unacceptable. IPFT, BJP, and Tipra Motha are contesting the Village Council General Election together as an alliance. Such acts of aggression directly undermine the very spirit of our unity. Political violence must stop immediately in every nook and corner of the state. I urge all party workers and supporters to maintain peace, uphold the integrity of our alliance, and ensure a safe, democratic election process,” he wrote in a social media post. 40, Akhaura Road, Agartala 799 001, Tripura, INDIA.

US inflation continues to make progress and we expect core personal consumption expenditures inflation to fall near 2% in 2027. Temporary drivers such as tariffs, AI shortages, energy price passthrough, and portfolio management fees are likely to subside while structural drivers such as wage and housing inflation remain subdued. Fed pricing has turned more hawkish, even as inflation and labor data has softened. Ambiguity around the new Chair’s reaction function may raise rate volatility in the near-term as there is more uncertainty in each meeting. title: Vikings & Legends Global Announce U.S. Bank Stadium Enhancements for 2026 - Minnesota Vikings
content: EAGAN, Minn. — The Minnesota Vikings and Legends Global are introducing a series of technology enhancements for the 2026 season at U.S. Bank Stadium. The changes, which include innovative entry procedures and an upgraded retail experience, are designed to make every visit, from arrival through departure, seamless for fans. Descriptions and links to video tutorials for each stadium enhancement are below. Open the Gates: Faster, Frictionless Security Screening U.S. Bank Stadium has enhanced the fan arrival experience with the installation of new OpenGate security screening technology at every entry point. The advanced contactless system allows guests to move through security screening without removing items from their pockets or having approved bags physically inspected, helping create a faster and more convenient entry process while enhancing stadium security. The clear bag policy that limits the size of bags allowed in the venue remains in effect. After trialing the technology in limited fashion during the 2025 season, the Vikings are expanding Vikings Express Pass, a voluntary touchless entry program powered by biometric authentication technology. The optional program allows enrolled guests to enter through designated lanes and eliminates the need to scan individual tickets or present a mobile device at the gate. Fans simply walk through the entry lane while their full allotment of tickets are automatically validated, reducing wait times and creating a seamless and efficient arrival experience when paired with the stadium's touchless security screening. Seven touchless entry lanes are available at five gate locations across the stadium, including the Legacy Gate, CFMOTO Gate, Ticketmaster Gate, Ecolab Gate and Upper 3M Gate. Participation is completely voluntary, and traditional ticket-scanning options remain available for all guests. Interested fans can sign up in advance here. Fans shopping at the Vikings Locker Room Store on the main concourse will enjoy a faster and more convenient checkout experience with the introduction of RFID self-checkout technology. The new system allows guests to simply place selected merchandise into a checkout station, where RFID technology instantly identifies all items at once and displays the purchase total for payment. The process eliminates the need to scan items individually, helping reduce lines and create a seamless shopping experience. In 2026, the Minnesota Vikings welcomed CFMOTO and TCL as new partners and expanded the team's longstanding relationship with 3M. As part of these new and expanded partnerships, several key locations throughout U.S. Bank Stadium have been updated. Fans entering the stadium will now find the CFMOTO Gate, Lower 3M Gate and Upper 3M Gate, while premium seating sections V1-V5 are now part of the TCL Club. Additional enhancements throughout the stadium include the introduction of the Miller Lite Bar on the main concourse and an expanded partnership with Factory Motor Parts, which now serves as the entitlement sponsor of the stadium parking garage. Guests are encouraged to review stadium maps, mobile tickets and Know Before You Go communications prior to arrival to ensure a smooth gameday experience. title: Goldman Stock Gains 38.6% in a Year: Buy Now or Wait for a Pullback? - TradingView
content: Shares of The Goldman Sachs Group GS have gained 38.6% in the past year, outperforming the industry’s rise of 26.1%. Its peers, Morgan Stanley MS and JPMorgan’s JPM shares rose 46.2% and 22.6%, respectively, over the same time frame. With such strong momentum, investors may be wondering whether to buy the GS stock now or wait for a better entry point. To help answer this question, let us take a closer look at the key factors driving Goldman’s growth and assess whether the stock still has room to run. Merger and acquisition (M&A) advisory remains a key competitive strength for Goldman. Winning mandates on large transactions not only supports advisory revenues but can also generate opportunities across financing, underwriting and other client businesses. Recent league-table rankings highlight that strength. Goldman was the only adviser in South and Central America to exceed $10 billion in aggregate deal value during the first half of 2026, according to GlobalData. It also ranked first among North American M&A advisers by deal value, advising on $437.7 billion in transactions. The favorable M&A backdrop led Goldman to deliver strong results. GS’s IB fees rose 52% year over year in the first half of 2026, driven by higher advisory, equity underwriting and debt underwriting revenues amid improving capital markets activity. Management also sounded constructive about the operating environment following the second-quarter results. CEO David Solomon highlighted accelerating momentum across the company’s businesses and pointed to strong client demand for Goldman to advise on major strategic transactions. Management noted that the investment banking backlog reached its highest level in five years, including a record advisory backlog, supported by robust strategic M&A activity, AI-related capital formation and stronger financing demand. Goldman is undertaking an ambitious, firmwide artificial intelligence (AI) transformation aimed at boosting fee income, improving productivity and expanding long-term operating leverage. The initiative spans its core businesses, including trading, investment banking, asset management and internal operations, positioning AI as a central growth driver. In July, Yahoo Finance, citing Reuters, reported that Goldman Sachs Asset Management had launched AlphaAI, an artificial intelligence-focused investment platform. The initiative underscores the firm's conviction that AI will emerge as a significant driver of investment opportunities and returns across both public and private markets. Earlier, Goldman partnered with Anthropic on a $1.5-billion initiative designed to accelerate AI adoption across hundreds of portfolio companies. At the center of Goldman’s transformation are two major initiatives — One Goldman Sachs 3.0, or OneGS 3.0, and the GS AI Assistant program. OneGS 3.0 is a multi-year effort to integrate AI into the firm’s core operating model rather than treat it as a standalone technology. The program focuses on simplifying workflows, modernizing infrastructure and supporting scalable growth through shared platforms, standardized processes and higher-quality data. The GS AI Assistant is expected to further improve employee productivity by helping professionals analyze information, generate content and complete routine tasks more efficiently. As adoption expands, the platform could reduce manual workloads and allow employees to devote more time to client engagement, decision-making and higher-value activities. Management has expressed strong confidence in AI’s long-term potential. Although spending on AI, data and digital infrastructure may keep expenses elevated in the near term, the investments could generate meaningful productivity gains and help the firm move toward its medium-term efficiency ratio target of 60%. GS streamlining efforts have been underway for some time as it retreats from the underperforming consumer banking ventures. Under CEO David Solomon, GS has embarked on a deliberate transformation to exit non-core consumer banking and double down on the divisions wherein Goldman maintains a clear competitive advantage. In sync with its restructuring efforts, in August 2026, Goldman agreed to acquire NEOS Investments. The acquisition will add $30 billion in assets across NEOS's 19 options-based income ETFs to Goldman Sachs Asset Management's existing $40 billion in income and outcome-oriented options-based ETF solutions. Once complete, the deal will make Goldman Sachs Asset Management the eighth-largest active ETF provider. In April 2026, GS acquired Innovator Capital Management, expanding its active ETF capabilities as part of a broader strategy to build durable revenue streams through diversified asset and wealth management offerings. In the same month, Goldman completed the divestiture of its Polish asset management business, Goldman Sachs TFI, to ING Bank Slaski, further streamlining its asset management operations. In the third quarter of 2025, the company transitioned the General Motors credit card program. These moves demonstrate a well-thought-out exit, allowing the company to reallocate capital and attention toward higher-margin, more scalable businesses like Global Banking and Markets, and the asset and wealth management divisions. Goldman maintains a fortress balance sheet, with the Tier 1 capital ratios well above regulatory requirements. This financial strength allows it to return capital to its shareholders aggressively through buybacks and a healthy dividend yield. As of June 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents were $187 billion, while deposits totaled $558 billion. Total unsecured debt (comprising long-term and short-term borrowings) was $438 billion, of which only $90 billion was near-term borrowings. Following the Federal Reserve’s 2026 stress test, the company increased its quarterly common stock dividend by 11% to $5 per share. The company also has a share repurchase plan in place. In the first quarter of 2025, the board approved a share repurchase program of up to $40 billion of common stock. As of June 30, 2026, Goldman had $21.6 billion worth of shares available under authorization. Supported by Goldman’s robust liquidity and capital levels, its shareholder payout activities appear sustainable. Analysts are bullish on GS. Over the past 60 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 and 2027 earnings has been revised upward. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Goldman’s 2026 and 2027 earnings implies year-over-year growth of 34.2% and 4.9%, respectively. The GS stock currently trades at a premium to the industry. The stock is trading at a forward price/earnings (P/E) of 14.58X above the industry average of 14.14X. Its peers JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are trading at a P/E of 14.47X and 16.76X, respectively. Goldman appears well-positioned to sustain its growth momentum, supported by strength in investment banking, a robust M&A pipeline, AI-led productivity initiatives, and continued expansion in asset and wealth management. Strategic streamlining, solid liquidity and healthy capital levels further support shareholder returns through dividends and share repurchases. While the stock trades at a modest premium to the industry, improving earnings estimates and strong business momentum help justify the valuation. Given its favorable earnings outlook, leading investment banking franchise and disciplined capital allocation, the GS stock offers an attractive investment opportunity at current levels. title: BMW Motorrad launches new F 450 GS in South Korea, starting at W12.5m - 헤럴드경제
content: BMW Motorrad, the motorcycle division of BMW, announced Tuesday it is launching the BMW New F 450 GS premium adventure motorcycle in South Korea. The BMW New F 450 GS is an entirely new model designed to bring the GS series' signature on- and off-road riding experience to a wider range of riders through a lighter frame and more accessible handling. In terms of design, the front features full LED headlights with an X-shaped daytime running light, combined with a sharply forward-swept nose and dynamic body lines that give the motorcycle an unmistakably bold GS family look. The bodywork incorporates GS-defining design elements throughout, including the signature "beak," "tooth" and distinctive flyline. The sleek silhouette running from the fuel tank through the seat to the rear emphasizes a light, dynamic character, while the center section of the 14-liter fuel tank is slimmed down to allow riders to brace the bike securely with their knees whether seated or standing. Built on a curb weight of 178 kilograms and an entirely new chassis, the BMW New F 450 GS delivers agile yet stable riding performance. Both front and rear suspension offer 180 millimeters of travel, covering a wide range of on- and off-road conditions. The front uses a 43mm inverted telescopic fork, while the rear employs an aluminum double swingarm with a central spring strut. Lightweight cast aluminum wheels — 19 inches at the front and 17 inches at the rear — paired with dual-sport tires round out the setup for stable riding across varied surfaces. The BMW New F 450 GS is powered by a 420cc parallel-twin engine producing 48 hp and a maximum torque of 4.4 kg·m. The powertrain was developed from the outset specifically for the F 450 GS, engineered to deliver strong performance and sharp responsiveness despite its compact, lightweight construction. A new six-speed gearbox comes standard across all trims, along with Shift Assistant Pro, which enables quick upshifts and downshifts without operating the clutch lever in most riding situations. The GS Trophy trim of the BMW New F 450 GS comes standard with the new Easy Ride Clutch (ERC), a system that uses a precision centrifugal mechanism to automatically engage and disengage the clutch based on engine speed. The BMW New F 450 GS also offers four riding modes to handle a variety of surfaces and conditions: Rain, Road, Enduro and Enduro Pro. Safety electronics include ABS Pro for stable braking through corners, Dynamic Traction Control (DTC) to suppress rear-wheel slip, Dynamic Brake Control (DBC) to prevent unintended throttle input during hard braking, and engine drag torque control to reduce rear-wheel slide during deceleration. The cockpit features a 6.5-inch TFT color display with sharp graphics and excellent visibility. Riders can intuitively check key riding data — including speed, engine rpm, DTC status, braking force and lean angle — and easily select the appropriate riding mode for any environment. The BMW New F 450 GS goes on sale in South Korea in two trims: Exclusive and GS Trophy, priced at 12.5 million won ($9,310) and 13.5 million won, respectively. Meanwhile, BMW Motorrad recently launched the BMW Motorrad Vantage app, an integrated lifestyle platform for motorcycle customers. BMW Vantage, first introduced in 2020 as the automotive industry's first lifestyle platform, offers a wide range of services spanning mobility, travel, culture and education, built around "Vantage Coin," a membership points currency exclusive to customers.

title: Mailbag: Harrison Smith’s Return; Vikings Roster Mechanics; 2026 Week 1 Arrives - Minnesota Vikings
content: Do you have a comment or question? Send it to the Mailbag. Every Monday we'll post several comments and/or questions. Click here to submit a comment or question to Mailbag. Remember to include your name and town in the email. If Twitter / X is your jam, you can send a question to me that way as well. The Hitman returneth — and just in time for the 2026 regular season. Harrison Smith and the Vikings on Saturday agreed to terms for the 2012 first-round pick to return to Minnesota for his 15th NFL season. Smith is back at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center this morning. The Vikings will open their 66th slate by hosting the Green Bay Packers at 3:25 p.m. (CT) Sunday at U.S. Bank Stadium. Assuming he suits up, it will be the 27th Border Battle for Smith (out of 132 in the series). Memorably, the two teams met to conclude the 2025 season at the same venue, and Smith (just in case he didn't return) and C.J. Ham (who was playing in his final game) received tributes from the crowd. The Vikings also will be wearing their Classic uniforms for the second straight home game against the Packers. The rivalry rarely needs hype, but as an additional boost, CBS' THE NFL TODAY will be broadcasting on CBS from the Vikings Legacy Ship before the noon slate of games. Folks are encouraged to join the atmosphere, regardless of whether they have game tickets. The same goes for the free Vikings Kickoff Concert featuring Cole Swindell, which is scheduled to start at 1 p.m. in The Commons. View photos of the Vikings 53-man roster as of Sep. 5, 2026. I had a good idea Harrison Smith would return. But the silence was causing a slight vibration in my foundation. I was wondering if he wanted to skip camp and all the offseason rigor and save his health for "real" football. I know in the past some players have prolonged the decision to return for that reason. No matter now. He has experience on the field and the ability to influence and educate those around him. I figure Coach Flores is downright giddy like all of Viking Nation. Thank you, Hitman! We love you! Now start lighting people up! It was admittedly and unquestionably weird to produce the Vikings Yearbook and Playbook editions for Training Camp and the first preseason game without including Smith. He was in his third Vikings season when I started here, so it's become quite routine to see him patrolling the defense and doing un-routine things, adding to his candidacy for the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Smith's knowledge of Defensive Coordinator Brian Flores' system, from the meeting room to his ability to bring it to life on the field should benefit young players who have joined an impressive core of veterans. Maybe he heard how much fun the crew had during those joint practices with Baltimore? We'll probably hear from Smith in a media session later this week, but I'd imagine he's kept up a strong training plan. The 53-man roster is now set, so the focus has to be on beating the Green Bay Packers on Sept. 13 at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. How will Kyler Murray and the "Minnesota Moving Company" handle the Green Bay Packers defense? Everybody is talking about how good Kyler Murray, our WRs and TEs will be in 2026. That only happens if our OL plays well and stays healthy. I did not see much of anything this past preseason to make me confident, except for maybe a few plays against the Giants. If we can't run the ball on third-and-2, or Kyler is on his back or running for his life against the blitz, it all won't matter. It all comes down to our OL (again) so LETS GO!!! SKOL It's hard to say how any season will go, but the Vikings should be able to answer some internal and external questions right out of the gate. Murray is looking forward to making his first start for Minnesota after playing just nine offensive snaps in this year's preseason opener at the New York Giants. He and the Vikings first-team offense pivoted to Week 1 preparations when training camp finished. The starting offensive line hasn't appeared in a game together since popping an 18-yard run by Aaron Jones, Sr., on the inaugural snap of the preseason. The group was able to log substantial work in individual and team drills when Minnesota hosted Baltimore for joint practices. While there are sure to be plenty of eyeballs on Murray, I'm among those highly intrigued in seeing what the revamped run game looks like. I want to learn whether the offensive line is able to play on Green Bay's side of the line of scrimmage on run plays and provide a pocket that will keep Murray from needing to dip into his scrambling ability too often. Spoiler alert, we'll have a feature on Vikings.com this week about the revamped running game, so be on the lookout for that in addition to other content to get you prepared for the game. The group expected to play the most on Sunday has a very limited sample size in the public view this year, but I get the feeling the offensive line is eager to harvest the results of its hard work. I really like former Vikings running back Zavier Scott. He has a great story and he runs hard. I was surprised when he didn't make the team, but now I understand that they planned to add him to the practice squad if he cleared waivers. Unfortunately, the Bears are going to sign him. The team gambled and lost, but that's the way the system works. My question is this; do you think teams, especially division rivals, pick up players like that to pick their brains on what their previous teams offense and defense looks like? I suppose it's legal but, how does a team protect their secrets? — Mike Schuffenhauer, Fan from North Minneapolis since 1969 Scott is a player all Vikings fans can feel good about wishing well as he continues his career, except for any opportunities directly against the Vikings. He runs hard and works even harder, and he daily walks the walk of his faith. I'm sure Chicago's primary interest in signing him was to add a good, young player to its practice squad, but there could be a situation where the Bears try to learn more about Minnesota's new run game or protection calls or play designs from Scott, which could provide a little help in preparing for Week 2 when Chicago would only have one game film to review when researching this year's approach. View the best photos of Vikings safety Harrison Smith throughout his career as he announced he will return for his 15th season in 2026. Please describe the various amounts of money that practice squad players make? What kind of latitude do NFL teams have with deals for practice squad players? Might some be guaranteed deals? And how does the game check change when a player is elevated to the active roster? We heard from Vikings General Manager Nolan Teasley last week in his first comments since reducing the roster to the 53-man limit and establishing the practice squad, which is capped at 16 (or 17 with one International Player Pathway participant). One thing that was clear in Teasley's comments is his appreciation for the practice squad and his holistic view of the roster as 70 instead of 53. The practice squad continues to evolve and creates opportunities for players to be readily available. The sizes of practice squads have increased substantially since Teasley launched his career with Seattle in 2013. Players on practice squads can be poached at any point if another team signs the player to its 53. The Rochester Democrat and Chronicle just reported on practice squad salaries last week and noted players with two or fewer accrued seasons receive $13,750 per week, which would total $247,500 if a player was on the practice squad an entire season without being elevated. Practice squad players with more experience can negotiate for a range between $18,350 and 22,850 per week. According to the NFL Operations Manuel, if a player is elevated for a regular-season game, he receives the "applicable minimum salary for a player with his number of credited seasons (prorated for one week of regular-season pay or the applicable postseason amount). Practice squad players can be elevated three times in one League Year. After that, a subsequent elevation would require placement on the 53-man Active/Inactive list. "The team must then waive or terminate his player contract before the player can be re-signed to the practice squad. If the player is re-signed to the practice squad this way, the player is again eligible to be elevated for the previously mentioned maximum of three games." Ownership and the upper end of the team are really impressive, as are many of the position coaches, and both the offensive and defensive coordinators. It may not happen this year, but if they are able to keep this nucleus in place for two years, they are going to be very hard to beat as they win their first Super Bowl. We'll close today with a bit of positivity from Bruce. There have been intentional decisions backed by sound processes (player evaluations, analytics and reason) in trying to build the best possible team. Every squad will be challenged by something in the course of an NFL season, and some teams appear to have better fortunes than others with regard to injuries or bounces of the football. title: Karol G electrifies El Paso's Sun Bowl with 2 sold-out nights - elpasotimes.com
content: Fans arrived in their “Tripicoqueta” outfits for Karol G's concert at the Sun Bowl, bringing the colorful aesthetic surrounding the singer's latest era to life. Warm oranges, pinks and yellows, mixed with earthy browns and neutrals, while floral prints and accessories completed the tropical style. Karol G celebrated her biggest hits with El Paso fans for two nights, Sept. 5-6, at Sun Bowl Stadium. The Colombian superstar is on a worldwide tour with "Viajando Por el Mundo Tropitour" hitting many U.S. cities, including Chicago, New York and Miami. Becky G was the special guest for the El Paso shows. El Pasoan Sandy Jordan attended the concert with her daughter, Natalia Cruz, and her mom, Celia Cruz, who introduced both of them to Karol G’s music. “My mom, she’s like a top fan of Karol G,” Jordan said. “It’s just a special moment. We get to have this experience together, like all three of us, three generations.” Jordan said she had waited a long time for the concert and was excited to see Karol G perform for the first time. Fans delighted in hearing hits like "Latina Foreva," OKI DOKI," and “Tá OK". El Paso native Greg Gonzalez of Cigarettes After Sex made a surprise appearance during the concert, joining Karol G onstage to perform their duet, “Después De Ti.” They previously performed the song together at Coachella earlier this year. Her shows are as much a feast for the eyes as for the ears, featuring dazzling light displays, fireworks, and towering flames. She is one of the most in-demand Latin artists, having expanded her tour from 39 cities to more than 60 stadium shows. Multiple cities sold out their initial dates within hours, prompting second, third and fourth stadium shows. For El Pasoan Laura Chavez, it was her second time seeing Karol G perform live, but she was happy to see the singer in her hometown of El Paso. “I’m very grateful that we have the opportunity to have her here,” Chavez said in Spanish. “Her music represents us because it reflects what we feel,” Chavez said in Spanish. “Sometimes we don’t talk about those feelings, and through music, we’re able to let them out.” Chavez attended the concert with Berenice Miravete, who traveled from Colorado with her daughter, Genesis Galindo, for Galindo’s first concert. title: Hur Sae-hong charts GS Caltex’s path beyond refining - The Korea Herald
content:
Business Hur Sae-hong charts GS Caltex’s path beyond refining Published : Sept. 7, 2026 - 15:27:55
Updated : Sept. 7, 2026 - 18:01:39 Vice chair outlines GS Caltex’s lower-carbon transformation in McKinsey interview Amid sweeping changes in global energy markets, GS Caltex Vice Chair Hur Sae-hong seeks to move South Korea’s energy and chemical company beyond its decades-old focus on refining volumes toward higher-value, lower-carbon businesses. Hur outlined his vision in McKinsey & Co.’s “Leading Asia” interview series and its centennial book, “Shapers & Founders: The Untold Stories of Asia’s Extraordinary Owner-CEOs.” He was featured alongside other Korean business leaders from companies including HD Hyundai and MBK Partners. A fourth-generation member of GS Group’s founding family, Hur spent more than 18 years working in Japan, the US and Singapore for companies including IBM and Chevron. Those experiences helped shape a management philosophy that combines global adaptability with what he describes as traditional Korean humility. At its center is “we-dership,” Hur’s term for leadership built collectively. The idea calls on executives to “lead from the top, but move together,” with teamwork underpinning the company’s ambition to remain competitive for the next century. GS Caltex, Korea’s first private oil refiner, operates the world’s fourth-largest single-site refinery. The company prospered for decades on surging energy demand across Asia, but slowing global growth and the risk of excess supply have challenged its traditional volume-led model. “How can we maintain a growth path on a quality basis to ensure we remain sustainable for the future?” Hur said. His answer is what GS Caltex calls its “Deep Transformation Journey,” built around three pillars of transformation: business, digital and artificial intelligence, and green transformation. Business transformation, which the company calls BX, seeks to overhaul its mindset, culture and organizational structure. Digital and AI transformation, or DAX, focuses on building capabilities internally, including retraining and refining petrochemical engineers through an in-house digital academy. Green transformation, or GX, seeks to shift the company’s portfolio toward lower-carbon growth areas. These include sustainable aviation fuel, bio-based marine fuel, circular plastics, clean hydrogen, and carbon capture, utilization and storage. Hur is also pushing for GS Caltex to build what he calls a “black-box advantage” — an internal combination of work processes, organizational capabilities and corporate culture that competitors would struggle to replicate. Investing in emerging green businesses carries substantial risk, but Hur argues that standing still poses an even greater threat. He describes the status quo as “a killer of sustainable growth.” To manage that risk, GS Caltex uses marginal abatement cost curves to assess projects according to their cost and emissions-reduction potential, prioritizing lower-risk opportunities. Hur is also trying to preserve startuplike agility within a large corporation. A newly created "business council" brings senior executives together to lead cross-company strategic projects that might otherwise remain confined within individual business units. Named one of Stanford Graduate School of Business’ “Centennial Alumni Catalysts” in 2025, Hur said the success of the strategy would ultimately be judged by measurable results. “For me, sustainability means fundamentally rebalancing our portfolio toward lower-carbon businesses,” he said. “In the end, I believe the only way to demonstrate this commitment is through outcomes, not words.” S. title: JADES-GS-z14-0, a galaxy discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope, already contained oxygen less than 300 million years after the Big Bang — a finding confirmed by ALMA, suggesting generations of massive stars had already been born, lived and - spacedaily.com
content:
ALMA detected ionised oxygen in a galaxy seen before the universe was 300 million years old, supporting rapid stellar enrichment while leaving its exact history open. By Deep Field
·
Edited by
												Lachlan Brown JADES-GS-z14-0 already contained oxygen when the universe was less than 300 million years old. Two teams reported the detection using ALMA, the telescope array in Chile, in studies publicised in March 2025. Webb had discovered the galaxy and established its extreme distance; ALMA added a clear chemical signature and a much more precise redshift. The oxygen implies that stars had already made heavier elements and released them into surrounding gas. The suggestion of successive generations of massive stars is physically plausible, but the observation does not count those generations or identify individual ancient supernovae. In NASA’s May 2024 discovery account, Stefano Carniani and Kevin Hainline described almost ten hours of observations with Webb’s Near-Infrared Spectrograph. The spectrum placed the galaxy at a redshift near 14, within the first few hundred million years of cosmic history. Webb’s Mid-Infrared Instrument supplied another clue. The galaxy was brighter at longer wavelengths than a simple continuation of its shorter-wavelength light would suggest. The team interpreted that excess as evidence for strong emission from ionised gas, including hydrogen and oxygen. That was an inference from brightness measured across a wavelength band. Detecting an individual oxygen line would provide a more specific test. Sander Schouws and colleagues, writing in The Astrophysical Journal, reported a 6.6-sigma detection of the [O III] 88-micrometre line. The notation refers to oxygen atoms that have lost two electrons. Expansion stretched this far-infrared emission into the millimetre wavelengths that ALMA measures. The line gave a redshift of 14.1793, with an uncertainty of 0.0007. That greatly narrowed the earlier Webb estimate while keeping the galaxy firmly within the era before the universe reached 300 million years of age. Carniani’s team, in Astronomy & Astrophysics, obtained a closely matching redshift of 14.1796 from its analysis of the oxygen emission. As ESO’s announcement explains, two teams reached the detection through independent analyses of ALMA data. This agreement strengthens the interpretation of the signal; it is not evidence from two different galaxies. This is ionised oxygen in galactic gas, not a detection of a breathable atmosphere. The early universe began with matter dominated by hydrogen and helium. Substantial oxygen enrichment requires later nuclear processing in stars. ESO describes the sequence behind the finding: stars produce heavier elements, then spread them through their surroundings when they die. The relevant clock is very different from the Sun’s. NASA’s guide to stellar types explains that stellar lifetimes vary enormously with mass. Massive stars consume their fuel quickly and can complete their lives on timescales of millions of years. Their evolving interiors produce heavier nuclei, and supernova explosions can eject enriched material into space. A galaxy therefore does not need billions of years to acquire oxygen. It needs stars to form early enough, some of them to evolve rapidly, and their products to reach the gas being observed. The abundance and distribution of that material depend on how much is produced, mixed, retained or expelled. In our earlier discussion of why Webb’s apparently mature galaxies do not automatically imply impossible ages, the distinction was between chemical development and elapsed time. Oxygen provides evidence of processing. It is not a stopwatch with a fixed number of stellar generations marked on it. Schouws’s team combined the ALMA measurement with Webb information and gas-emission models to estimate a heavy-element abundance roughly five to twenty per cent of the Sun’s. Carniani’s modelling favoured about seventeen per cent of the solar value. These are estimates of chemical abundance relative to a reference composition, not claims that seventeen per cent of the galaxy’s mass is oxygen. The oxygen detection is firmer than every detail of the reconstructed history. Carniani and colleagues also considered whether earlier outflows had removed gas. Such an interpretation depends on estimates of stellar mass, gas content and star-formation history. The authors’ proposed history should remain distinct from the directly measured emission line. NASA dates the formation of our Solar System to about 4.6 billion years ago. The cloud that formed it already included elements made in previous stars. JADES-GS-z14-0 shows that this broader process of stellar manufacture and enrichment was operating far earlier, near the beginning of galaxy formation. The comparison is chronological. It does not establish that oxygen detected in this remote galaxy became part of the Sun or Earth. Our coverage of Webb’s challenge to early galaxy-formation models described the wider problem: bright, active systems appear early, and explaining them requires careful treatment of star formation, gas, dust and feedback. A measured chemical signature adds another constraint to that work. For JADES-GS-z14-0, Carniani’s team identified deeper Webb spectroscopy as a route to a better carbon-to-oxygen measurement. Comparing those elements would help test which stellar populations enriched the gas and how quickly that enrichment occurred. This article is for general information and reflection. title: Korean builders race to invest in Robocon to automate rebar work - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: Major builders pour funds into Robocon as labor shortages spur a push for automated rebar handling GS Engineering & Construction and Hoban Construction also invested in Robocon, a robot-based construction automation corporations. Construction companies suffering from labor shortages and rising building costs are moving to secure related technology to replace repetitive and hazardous tasks such as rebar processing with robots. On the 7th, according to the construction industry, the PlanH-XPLOR Green Smart City Venture Investment Partnership, funded by GS Engineering & Construction and Hoban Construction, acquired Robocon's convertible bonds (CB). A CB is a bond that can be converted into the issuing company's stock if certain conditions are met. The fund was jointly formed in 2024 by XPLOR Investment, the corporate venture capital (CVC) of GS Engineering & Construction, and PlanH Ventures, the Hoban Construction CVC. With a total size of 38.5 billion won, the National Land and Transport sector parent fund contributed 15 billion won, GS Engineering & Construction 11.5 billion won, Hoban Construction 2 billion won, and XPLOR Investment 500 million won, among others. A XPLOR Investment official said, "We decided from a strategic investment perspective that can boost productivity at construction sites and accelerate digital transformation, and considering investment revenue," adding, "Several institutions are showing interest in the pre-IPO stage of equity investment before listing, but no additional investment has been decided." Robocon was established in Nov. 2020 when the robotics business unit of Daehan Networks, an affiliate of the DaehanSteel group, was spun off. It develops automation solutions specialized for rebar processing, assembly, and transport. Its flagship solution, "ARON," automates processing steps such as rebar supply, cutting, and bending. According to Robocon, when producing 3,000 tons of rebar for building frames at a rebar processing plant, up to 30 people were previously needed, but introducing ARON can reduce the workforce to fewer than 10. The company said it can cut labor assigned to repetitive tasks and lower material loss that occurs during rebar processing. Robocon's automation solutions have also been adopted at overseas sites, including Singapore's Tuas Port and a project related to Taipei Airport in Taiwan, both built by Korean construction companies. Construction companies are investing in Robocon one after another to address labor shortages at sites and rising construction costs. Automating repetitive tasks that handle heavy materials, such as rebar transport and processing, can raise productivity while also reducing the workforce assigned to hazardous work. Earlier, Samsung C&T invested about 15 billion won in Robocon in 2023 through a fund managed by Samsung Venture Investment. It then secured a majority of board voting rights and, in the second half of the same year, included Robocon as a consolidation subsidiary. Following Samsung C&T, with GS Engineering & Construction and Hoban Construction joining the investment, competition among major builders to secure construction automation technology is entering full swing.

title: GS Caltex and SOOP Supers Trade Key Players to Address Needs - 조선일보
content: Setter Park Sa-rang joins GS Caltex, libero Yu Ga-ram moves to SOOP Supers in strategic roster adjustments [Sports Chosun Kim Young-rok Reporter] "I feel sorry and frustrated. But it was a necessary trade for the team…" The voice of Lee Young-taek, GS Caltex head coach, was filled with regret over the phone. Sending away a 21-year-old outside hitter he had nurtured with care since his arrival couldn’t have been easy. GS Caltex and SOOP Supers recently made a surprising trade. SOOP sent setter Park Sa-rang (23), selected first overall in the rookie draft when Pepper Savings Bank was founded, to GS Caltex, while GS Caltex sent libero Yu Ga-ram (21), whom they had been developing intensively, to SOOP. The trade aligned with GS Caltex’s concerns about filling the setter vacancy left by An Hye-jin (free agent) and SOOP’s need to reinforce their libero position, where only Han Da-hye remained as the starting player. Notably, this trade was finalized three days after GS Caltex’s media day. As the defending champion, having achieved an underdog victory last season led by Geisel Silva, the team’s setter issue was a hot topic at the event. Lee Young-taek explained, "We have starting setter Kim Ji-won, and we’ve worked hard to develop backup setters Lee Yoon-shin and Choi Yoon-young. We hired setter specialist coach Ishii Sugu-ru and had them train every night during the offseason. Since setters need experience, we focused on giving these two players more practice matches to build their skills." He added, "Their growth isn’t yet satisfactory, but we’ll keep developing them." However, just three days later, GS Caltex completed the trade to acquire setter Park Sa-rang. A GS Caltex official explained, "We’d been concerned about An Hye-jin’s vacancy, and SOOP reached out with a proposal. The trade filled both teams’ needs. Park Sa-rang is a solid backup for Kim Ji-won." Regarding Yu Ga-ram, the official sighed repeatedly, saying, "She was a player we’d developed so well…" Over the past two seasons, Yu played 64 matches and 213 sets as a defensive reinforcement outside hitter, backup libero, and serve-receive specialist. Last season, her reception efficiency was 36.3% (58/146), effectively supporting Han Su-jin (36.71%, 187/444). She was also seen as a rising franchise star alongside Yu Seo-yeon, Han Su-jin, and Oh Se-yeon. However, with starting libero Han Su-jin firmly established and 19-year-old Kim Hyo-im rapidly growing—even earning a spot on the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games team—the libero position became more stable. Among the three liberos, SOOP specifically targeted Yu Ga-ram. Through this trade, GS Caltex filled their setter vacancy with a proven player. In volleyball, the saying "the game is in the setter’s hands" underscores the difficulty of finding a setter as reliable as Park Sa-rang. Additionally, Kim Ji-won will become a free agent after this season, and An Hye-jin’s return remains uncertain. Even if she returns, her status as a free agent means GS Caltex cannot guarantee her return. Negotiating with two free-agent setters simultaneously would have been complicated, but acquiring Park Sa-rang resolved this. Lee Young-taek sighed, saying, "Yu Ga-ram was hard to let go." However, he added, "Kim Hyo-im grew faster than expected. She seized her opportunity and developed enough to join the Asian Games team. Kim Ji-won alone can’t handle a full season, and our other setters still need time. There were valid reasons for this trade." For SOOP, Park Sa-rang holds special significance as their first overall pick when Pepper Savings Bank was founded. Before the team’s acquisition, SOOP lost outside hitters Park Jeong-ah and Lee Han-bi, creating a vacancy. To address this, they traded their second-round rookie draft pick with Hyundai Engineering & Construction for Seo Ji-hye, and swapped Jung Sol-min with Industrial Bank of Korea (IBK) for Go Ui-jeong and another second-round pick. They also signed Jeon Sae-ah, released by Korea Expressway Corporation, adding depth to their outside hitter position. With Yu Ga-ram’s arrival, they reinforced their libero lineup beyond Han Da-hye and decided to operate with setters Lee Won-jeong and Park Su-bin. A SOOP official explained, "Han Da-hye is excellent, but injuries are a risk. Coach Kim Se-jin was concerned, and the trade with GS Caltex aligned perfectly. We believe Park Su-bin has higher growth potential." SOOP is also anticipating the rookie draft, which now allows overseas Korean players to participate. Audrey Park (24, Columbus Fury), a rising star expected to follow Kim Yeon-koung’s legacy, is a top prospect for all seven women’s volleyball teams. SOOP holds 35 out of 100 lottery balls, the second-highest after Jung Kwan Jang (30+8 balls) from HK, who acquired an additional first-round pick via a trade with PyeongAn. GS Caltex holds just one ball. The V-League will reconvene with fans on October 11, starting with the KOVO Cup in Yeosu.

title: No more Udta Gujarat? - Ahmedabad Mirror
content: Sep 07, 2026 06:00 AM | UPDATED: Sep 08, 2026 01:46 AM | 10 min read The state police on Sunday ordered the setting up of dedicated Anti-Narcotics Wings (ANWs) in every district and city, with the units to become operational within seven days.  Gujarat has witnessed large-scale drug seizures, with over 1.36 lakh kg of narcotic substances worth around Rs 13,600 crore seized in past five years. During this period, Gujarat Police registered more than 3,700 cases under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and arrested 5,346 accused. The new ANWs will strengthen the existing enforcement mechanism by creating dedicated teams at the district and city levels, complementing the state-level Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF). DGP GS Malik said the ANWs would function as a “Specialised Task Force” and work exclusively on NDPS-related crimes. No other duties will be assigned to the teams, allowing them to focus on drug peddlers, trafficking networks and habitual offenders. Each ANW will comprise eight personnel—one police inspector, one police sub-inspector, two ASIs/head constables and four police constables —and will have a dedicated vehicle. At the commissionerate level, Ahmedabad and Surat will have two units each, while Vadodara and Rajkot will have one each. District units will function under the direct supervision of the respective Superintendent of Police, while commissionerate units will work under the Joint or Additional Commissioner of Police. The ANWs will maintain continuous surveillance over drug peddlers and drug hotspots identified by the ANTF. They will also send proposals to CID Crime for preventive action under PIT-NDPS against habitual drug offenders. The new arrangement will supplement the existing role of local police, LCBs and SOGs in detecting NDPS cases. Gujarat has also introduced a Drug Reward Policy, making it the first state in the country to incentivise police personnel and informants who help apprehend drug networks. An out-of-turn promotion policy is also in place for personnel who perform high-risk duties during anti-narcotics operations. The police have developed AI-based ‘NARIT’ software to detect dark-web activities, financial trails and international links to drug networks. Scientific investigation is being undertaken to strengthen cases and improve conviction rates. De-addiction centres are being modernised to provide counselling and treatment, particularly to youth affected by substance abuse. title: Modular AI Data Centers Cut Construction Time to Six Months - Businesskorea
content: A prefabricated modular model that can dramatically reduce the construction time for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers is emerging as a new alternative in the industry. The approach aims to shorten construction timelines from the typical two years to six months or less, allowing infrastructure to begin operating before the performance of the latest graphics processing units (GPUs) deteriorates. LG Uplus said on Sept. 6 that it signed an agreement with GS E&C, Xi C&A, Gansam Architects & Partners and D&O CM to develop a standard model for prefabricated modular data centers (PMDCs). The agreement is significant in that companies with expertise spanning the entire data center lifecycle, from design and construction to operations, have joined forces with the goal of applying the model to actual projects. PMDCs are built by standardizing building structures and power and cooling systems, prefabricating them at a factory and then transporting them to a site for assembly. Since April, the participating companies have been developing a “new-build model” centered on a 100-megawatt (MW) hyperscale PMDC and a “retrofit model” that converts existing buildings into AI data centers. The biggest advantage of the model is its significantly shorter construction time. While conventional building-type data centers take about two years to complete, PMDCs can be completed in six months. As GPU replacement cycles accelerate, construction delays can lead directly to a decline in the value of computing infrastructure, making rapid deployment a key factor directly linked to investment efficiency. The model also offers advantages in quality control and scalability. Because major facilities are manufactured at factories and undergo testing in advance, it can minimize quality variations and the risk of rework that can occur during on-site construction. It also allows modules to be added incrementally as AI demand grows, enabling more flexible operations by expanding capacity as needed. The companies will divide responsibilities based on their respective areas of expertise to improve the model. LG Uplus will define technical requirements and validate the model based on its 27 years of data center operating experience, while GS E&C will handle constructability reviews and process optimization. Xi C&A will focus on power and cooling optimization, while Gansam Architects & Partners and D&O CM will oversee standard design and project management, respectively. Other South Korean companies are also moving to adopt modular construction methods. In March, LG CNS unveiled “AI Box,” a small-scale 1.2 MW data center equipped with 576 GPUs. SK Telecom is also developing a “prefab modular” solution in cooperation with global manufacturers to integrate the production of servers and power infrastructure. Securing power, however, remains a challenge separate from the speed of infrastructure construction. Because AI data centers consume enormous amounts of electricity, faster module production alone cannot accelerate the actual start of operations if grid connections are delayed. An industry official suggested that, given the trend of longer waiting periods for grid access, complementary measures combining energy storage systems (ESS) with intelligent energy management systems should be pursued in parallel.
